sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the four agents and the project data types. The header describes the file as orchestrating agents 3 to 6, which cover workstreams, dependencies, modules and timeline.
sections.why: Needed to build the pipeline from the agents and the shared data types.
sections.watch_out: The agent numbers in the header are the only record of their order, so keep them in step with the code if the pipeline changes.

sections.name: ContentGenerator (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the agents
sections.what: Stores the search engine and LLM object, then creates the four agents with the same API key and model. Each agent is given the same search engine so it can look up past proposals.
sections.why: Shares one set of settings and one search tool across all agents, so they behave consistently.
sections.watch_out: The code reads specific attributes from the LLM object, so a different LLM class without those attributes will fail at startup.

sections.name: ContentGenerator: generate_content
sections.title: Generating workstreams, dependencies and the first steps
sections.what: Reads explicit workstreams and the duration from the RFP. Then looks up similar past proposals to build workstreams, and uses them to find dependencies. Prints progress messages for each step.
sections.why: The RFP names are read but the learned list replaces them, so the explicit list has no effect. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The RFP's explicit workstream names are read and then dropped, so the final plan may miss them. Reasoning returned by these steps is ignored.

sections.name: ContentGenerator (part 3)
sections.title: Building modules, optimizing the timeline and returning the project
sections.what: For each workstream, builds its modules using the other workstreams and the RFP for context. Then the timeline optimizer rearranges work, using the target duration if one was given or the RFP duration otherwise. Finally it packages everything into a project and prints a summary.
sections.why: Modules are built one workstream at a time so each one gets its own focused request. The timeline step runs last because it needs the dependencies and modules.
sections.watch_out: Reasoning and optimization results are discarded here, so they cannot be reviewed later. Assigning modules to a workstream skips the duration check in the data model.

sections.name: ContentGenerator: get_evidence_summary
sections.title: Reporting how much past evidence was used
sections.what: Returns the number of past proposal matches each agent used, defaulting to zero if an agent did not record a number.
sections.why: Gives a quick check of how much history shaped the result.
sections.watch_out: The code comment says this could be improved, so the counts may always show zero. Confirm the agents record their counts before trusting the numbers.

summary: Runs the main content pipeline for a proposal: it turns the RFP text into workstreams, dependencies, modules and an optimized timeline, using past proposals as examples.
purpose: Coordinates four AI agents so that one call produces the full project structure from an RFP.
why: Likely reason: each agent handles one step, and this file ensures they run in the correct order and share the same search tool.
how: Creates four agents with the same API key and model. Pulls workstreams from the RFP and from past proposals. Then finds dependencies, builds modules for each workstream, optimizes the timeline, and returns the project.
inputs: The full RFP text, a project name, and an optional target duration in weeks. The LLM object must provide an API key and model name.
outputs: A ProjectStructure with workstreams, modules and dependencies. It also gives a summary of evidence counts from each agent.
risks: Explicit workstreams taken from the RFP are discarded, so the RFP's own list may be ignored. Agent reasoning and optimization results are computed and then thrown away.
debug: If the output lacks the RFP's workstreams, check whether explicit names were dropped. If the start fails, check that the LLM object has the expected key and model attributes. Watch the console messages for each agent's step.
